definitions.explanation: Trees planted along streets and roads for shade, beautification, and environmental purposes. A common feature of Japanese urban landscapes.

examples.japanese: {街路樹|がいろじゅ}の{葉|は}が{色|いろ}づいてきた。
examples.english: The leaves of the street trees have started changing color.

examples.japanese: この{通|とお}りの{街路樹|がいろじゅ}はイチョウです。
examples.english: The roadside trees on this street are ginkgo trees.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{街路樹|がいろじゅ}が{何本|なんぼん}も{倒|たお}れて、{道路|どうろ}が{通行止|つうこうど}めになった。
examples.english: Several street trees were knocked down by the typhoon, and the road was closed to traffic.

notes:
USAGE:
{街路樹|がいろじゅ} refers specifically to trees planted along roads as part of urban planning. Common species used as street trees in Japan include イチョウ (ginkgo), {桜|さくら} (cherry), and ケヤキ (zelkova).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {街路樹|がいろじゅ}の{並木|なみき} (row of street trees)
- {街路樹|がいろじゅ}を{植|う}える (to plant street trees)
- {街路樹|がいろじゅ}の{剪定|せんてい} (pruning of street trees)

RELATED WORDS:
- {並木道|なみきみち}: tree-lined road
- {植樹|しょくじゅ}: tree planting
- {緑地|りょくち}: green space
